Portland, OR

memories below

City of Roses

Oregon greeted me from a window seat. The Cascades unrolled beneath the wing in layers of blue, and a lone snow-capped volcano floated above the clouds. That afternoon I wandered through Lan Su Chinese Garden, where carved lattice doors opened onto a whitewashed courtyard of miniature trees. A koi glided beneath a burgundy shrub, and an office tower peeking over the wall reminded me that this garden sits in the middle of downtown. By evening I was down at the Willamette, watching the lift towers of the Hawthorne Bridge rise above a marina in the low sun.

The next day belonged to Washington Park, up the hill from downtown. The International Rose Test Garden was at peak bloom, every bed overflowing with blushing pinks, striped oranges, lavenders and buttery yellows, with the bees hard at work. It dates to 1917, when it became a safe haven for European rose hybrids during World War I. Portland has long called itself the City of Roses, and in early June the nickname needs no defending.

A short climb away, the Portland Japanese Garden slowed everything down. A moss-draped waterfall trickled through a ravine of ferns and azaleas. Bronze birds stood at the edge of a still pond, and a five-tiered stone lantern kept watch beneath the conifers. From a wooden veranda I looked out over raked gravel and little islands of moss. Elsewhere, a few weathered stones sat in white sand, and somehow that was enough to quiet the mind. At one point Mount Hood hovered above the downtown towers, still heavy with snow.

The day after, I wandered Hoyt Arboretum, where a circular garden sinks into a sweeping lawn ringed by conifers. Nearly two years later, in late May of 2023, I returned for a short visit with the Columbia River Gorge on the list. Bridal Veil Falls dropped in two tiers through a narrow, mossy ravine, and Multnomah Falls slid down a wall of ochre basalt in one long, thin plume. Both sit just off the old Columbia River Highway, so one morning covers them. The next day, back in the city, I followed a trail beneath towering redwoods, pointing the lens skyward. A city that keeps a snowy volcano on its skyline and redwoods in its parks is easy to love.
